# First slice

Historical initial slice. The user's later 3D request is implemented under [3D_PLAN.md](3D_PLAN.md) and [3D_CONTRACT.md](3D_CONTRACT.md); those supersede the CAD/3D exclusions below. Core provider and evidence rules remain in force.

Local-first single-process app. JPG/PNG and small PDFs are mandatory. FastAPI serves static UI and API. Render PDF pages with PDFium and send the rendered source images to Gemini/Decisions; always identify inspected pages. Persist bounded uploads only in ignored local runtime storage. No reference-building retrieval, CAD, 3D, auth, streaming, hosting or infrastructure expansion.

Authorized development exception: select the temporary OpenAI Responses adapter via AI_PROVIDER=openai while Gemini access is pending. It uses one structured sufficiency classification without a confidence score. The final sponsor demo uses AI_PROVIDER=gemini and native Gemini Decisions. All evidence and retry rules are shared; no automatic failover.

1. Bootstrap environment and establish API contract.
2. Independent plan/reliability review.
3. Backend: upload normalization, provenance, Gemini provider adapter, one sufficiency decision, one bounded unclear inspection, evidence-linked structured answers.
4. Frontend: source viewer, upload, ask, status, result/citation highlighting and clear operational errors.
5. Integration and independent implementation review; meaningful tests for unsupported answers, unclear handling, missing credentials, bad uploads, citation bounds and API failures.
6. Document and run the local workflow; live Gemini smoke test only when a Gemini credential is configured. No substitute provider without agreement.

The initial evidence gate is an experiment, not a correctness guarantee. Evaluate against standard Gemini using coverage, error among answered questions, unsupported answers, unnecessary abstention, latency and usage. Synthetic fixtures verify control flow, not model quality.
# API contract v1

Root owns this contract; agents coordinate before changes. JSON uses snake_case.

The implemented 3D extension is specified in [3D_CONTRACT.md](3D_CONTRACT.md). Upload also accepts uncompressed IFC up to25MiB, with `kind` and `scene_url` fields; health adds `max_ifc_mb:25`. Answers add `highlight_ids` and `model_evidence`; IFC uses source records rather than page images. Existing drawing fields below remain compatible.

## Endpoints
- `GET /api/health`: `{status:"ok",provider_ready:bool,model:str,decision_model:str,limits:{max_upload_mb:10,max_pages:5}}`. Readiness means credentials/config exist, not verified provider access. No secrets.
- `POST /api/documents` multipart `file` (JPG/PNG/PDF, max 10 MiB, max 5 pages; reject larger documents rather than silently truncate). Returns `{document_id,filename,pages:[{page:1,width,height,image_url}],warnings:[]}`. Images are re-encoded PNG, PDF pages rendered. Opaque server-generated IDs; no filesystem paths.
- `GET /api/documents/{id}/pages/{page}` returns preview PNG.
- `POST /api/ask` JSON `{document_id,question}`. Question trimmed, 1–2000 chars. Returns Answer below.
- Standard errors: `{detail:"safe actionable message"}`; validation errors may be FastAPI detail arrays. API failures are 502/503, not insufficiency. Missing documents 404.

## Answer
```
{
  "status": "answered|insufficient|unclear",
  "answer": "human readable factual answer or scoped limitation",
  "evidence": [{"page":1,"bbox":[0.1,0.2,0.4,0.5],"label":"Bedroom label","observation":"MH annotation"}],
  "missing_information": ["Ceiling height"],
  "next_action": "Upload a section drawing with height dimensions.",
  "proposal": null,
  "inspected_pages": [1],
  "gate": {"decision":"sufficient|insufficient|unclear","confidence":0.8},
  "inspection_passes": 1,
  "usage": {"input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":0,"latency_ms":0}
}
```
`bbox` is [left,top,right,bottom], normalized 0–1 in the original displayed page. Validate positive area and page existence. Proposal if present: `{text, basis:"explicit_assumption|reference",reference:null|string}`. No invented reference buildings. Model-generated evidence is an aid to inspection, not a verified detection guarantee. Scores are model signals, not probabilities of factual correctness. `gate.confidence` is nullable: OpenAI's temporary structured classification returns null instead of inventing a confidence score.

Provider selection: `AI_PROVIDER=gemini|openai`, default gemini. Health additionally returns `provider`, `provider_label`, `credential_env`, `gate_kind` (`gemini_decisions|structured_classification`). For OpenAI, `decision_model` is the same configured `OPENAI_MODEL` used to generate the three-way classification. Missing/invalid configuration fails explicitly; no automatic fallback. The final demo must select Gemini.

## Provider orchestration
One overall Decisions choice on source pages + question. `unclear` allows one bounded targeted second inspection (a real crop/higher-resolution source view), then rerun the same gate with expanded evidence. Do not re-ask identical input and call it inspection. Standard Gemini explains limitations or generates a structured answer against original sources; never turn a negative gate into a factual answer. A positive gate does not force an answer when generation reveals missing evidence. Answer citations must validate; absent/invalid evidence cannot be silently accepted. Operational errors never silently fall back to a different gate/provider. No hidden live mocks or fixtures.

Provider documentation verified 2026-11-14: https://aistudio.google.com/docs/decisions-api ; Python SDK requires >=3.2 for Decisions. REST endpoint https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/decisions. Latest selected stable answer model: gemini-3.8-flash, configurable. SDK/REST details must be verified, not invented.

Implementation bound: at most two gate calls, one crop-selection call and one answer/explanation call. The crop is appended to the original pages with its original coordinates; it is not a separate source. The answer generator may downgrade a sufficient gate, never promote an insufficient/unclear gate. Arithmetic uses a small internal schema (sum, product, difference, quotient with source-indexed operands); code computes the value. Operand interpretation and unit compatibility still require human inspection. No claim of geometric or semantic verification is implied.

## Delivered
- Native uncompressed IFC import: stable GlobalIds, STEP references, source properties/units, world meshes in metres, semantic catalog retained when geometry fails.
- Cached shared scene schema for IFC and image-derived objects. Browser Three.js orbit/zoom/pan, raycast selection, object inspector, answer highlighting and 0.1-opacity surroundings.

Focused reviewer rerun: 40 tests passed, no remaining acceptance blocker.

## Boundaries to retain
IFC limits: 25 MiB / 4,000 elements / one million triangles; drawing limits: 10 MiB / five pages. Inspector stores up to 48 primitive source properties; inference sees the first 12 with omission warnings. Unavailable fields in this bounded view do not prove absence from the original IFC. Counts describe the source model, not the physical building.

Image geometry and labels are fallible interpretations. Actual answers still inspect source pixels. No generated height/thickness is supplied to answering. alright lets discuss the deliverable of this branch.

I’d make this branch deliver **one complete voice interaction with a blueprint**: the user speaks a question, sees the transcription, and hears the answer while the tool displays its evidence and highlights.

The demo flow would be:

1. Upload a plan or IFC using the existing interface.
2. Press a microphone button and ask a question.
3. Google transcribes speech live into the question field.
4. Submit the transcript through the existing Blueprint question pipeline.
5. Show the answer and citations, then read the answer aloud using ElevenLabs.
6. Allow the user to stop playback and ask another question.

For the first version, I suggest **push-to-talk with an editable transcript and explicit submission**. That’s our design choice to make question boundaries predictable and avoid submitting misheard dimensions or room names. It adds a click and won’t demonstrate fully hands-free conversation; automatic submission and interruption can follow if that matters for the demo.

The branch would deliver:

- Microphone controls, live transcript, and clear listening/processing/speaking states.
- Server-side Google transcription and ElevenLabs speech adapters, with credentials kept out of the browser.
- Integration with the existing answer pipeline, preserving evidence requirements and insufficient/unclear responses.
- Text fallback when either voice service fails.
- Deterministic adapter tests, setup instructions, and a live end-to-end verification when credentials are available.

One choice to settle first: by **Google live transcription**, do you mean **Google Cloud Speech-to-Text streaming**, or **Gemini Live API transcription**? I’d default to Speech-to-Text for this flow because we already have a separate system responsible for answering blueprint questions.

can you adjust what transcribe understands, e.g. some room names are pretty hard to pronounce or are unlikely to be understood wihtout the transcription model knowing that its valid, so is there basically a straight forward path to increase the words the transcription model understands

content.text:
**Yes—there’s a straightforward path: supply the transcription model with a vocabulary of names from the current building.** No model training is needed.

Google supports this in both options:

- **Gemini Live transcription:** accepts a `custom_vocabulary` list containing room names, unusual words, and technical terms. [Google’s documentation](https://aistudio.google.com/docs/live-api/live-transcribe#custom-vocabulary-biasing)
- **Cloud Speech-to-Text:** supports phrase hints and custom classes, plus adjustable “boost” values to make particular terms more likely. Availability depends on the model and language. [Google’s adaptation guide](https://docs.cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/adaptation-model)

For Blueprint, I’d propose this flow:

1. Extract room names from the IFC properties or labels read from the drawing.
2. Include those names when starting the transcription session.
3. Allow user-defined aliases—for example, “plant room” referring to the room labelled “Talotekniikka.”
4. Keep the transcript editable when a name is still misunderstood.

Vocabulary hints help the recognizer choose an unusual name when the audio sounds like it. **Aliases are a separate application feature:** they let someone use an easier name and still refer to the correct room.

This improves recognition without guaranteeing it; excessive bias can also produce a room name that wasn’t spoken. We should compare the same recordings with and without hints, including questions that don’t mention any listed room. [Google’s boost guidance](https://docs.cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/adaptation-model#boost_basics)

I’d include **vocabulary specific to the uploaded building** in this branch’s deliverable. The documented Gemini Live support also means this requirement doesn’t force us to use Cloud Speech-to-Text.

# Blueprint QA — hackathon instructions

## Scope
Build a local, lean application: upload JPG/PNG/PDF or IFC, ask a construction-plan question, inspect evidence and an interactive Three.js model. Current scope includes explicitly depicted floors via building description → deterministic IfcOpenShell generation → derived IFC → viewer. Read docs/RECONSTRUCTION_V2_PLAN.md and docs/RECONSTRUCTION_V2_CONTRACT.md, which supersede the single-floor slice. Defer unseen/invented floors, DXF/SVG/DWG, Blender/cloud rendering, auth, database and multi-agent runtime.

## Workflow
- Before introducing self-imposed constraints, explicitly communicate what they restrict, why they are needed, whether they are an external requirement or our design choice, and how they might block valid inputs or the demo. Prefer the smallest justified set for this hackathon. Do not silently introduce arbitrary caps or turn this into a blanket approval bureaucracy.
- Read docs/PLAN.md, docs/CONTRACT.md and docs/HANDOFF.md before changing behavior.
- Setup: `bash scripts/bootstrap.sh`. Run: `bash scripts/dev.sh`. Check: `bash scripts/test.sh`. Diagnose: `.venv/bin/python scripts/doctor.py`. Make targets are optional aliases when make is installed.
- Python 3.12+, FastAPI, plain HTML/CSS/JS, server-side Gemini (final demo) or explicit temporary OpenAI adapter. `AI_PROVIDER=gemini|openai`; default Gemini, never auto-failover. One process; no frontend build tool.
- Dependencies live in requirements.in; requirements.txt is the reproducible resolved lock. Coordinate dependency changes with the orchestrator.
- Use `.venv/bin/python`; do not modify system Python. Local sandbox may fail with bwrap: use approved escalated calls if required.
- Never print or commit `.env*` secrets, uploads, provider request bodies, or dataset answers. `.env.example` contains placeholders only.
- Use injected fake providers for deterministic tests. Never present fixture answers as real inference. API failures are operational errors, not evidence-insufficiency judgments.

## Product invariants
- One overall source-sufficiency gate: sufficient / insufficient / unclear. Inspect original source material, not only a model summary.
- Allow derivations with supported inputs. No invented dimensions as facts; no model confidence advertised as accuracy.
- Unclear gets at most one targeted additional inspection; unresolved stays unclear.
- Drawing answers cite normalized page/region evidence; IFC answers cite inspected GlobalId/property records. Unknown source references fail validation. Unreliable object mappings retain source evidence without highlighting.
- Genuine source IFC counts use the complete semantic catalog, including geometry-less objects. Generated IFC is always drawing-derived, including after reopening: restore original pages, inferred status and assumptions; never run native factual IFC shortcuts on it. Unknown scale uses an explicit context-dependent display unit, not measured metres. Supported calibration does not make assumed heights or generated geometry factual evidence.
- Missing information is scoped to inspected material. Similar-building ideas/defaults are explicitly proposals; never factual evidence about this building.
- Ground-truth questions.jsonl is evaluation-only, never runtime context.
- Gate sufficiency does not establish answer correctness. Check references and calculations; test confident failures too.

## Collaboration
The root agent is the orchestrator and owns architecture, contracts, environment and integration. Delegate bounded tasks to a planner, an independent plan reviewer, backend/frontend implementers, and an independent implementation reviewer. Reviewers must not review their own implementation as the independent review.

1. **Plan:** The planner proposes the smallest hackathon-sized implementation, explicit exclusions, file ownership, dependencies and testable acceptance criteria.
2. **Plan review loop:** The plan reviewer identifies blocking gaps, unnecessary scope and missing checks. The planner revises the plan and responds to each finding; the reviewer checks the revision. Allow at most two review rounds, then the orchestrator resolves remaining disagreements using evidence or scope reduction. Begin dependent implementation only after planning blockers are resolved. Do not reopen settled scope without new evidence or a user-requested change.
3. **Implementation:** Assign backend/frontend work with clear file ownership and a shared contract. Implementers edit only assigned paths, communicate contract changes first, and do not revert another agent's changes. Parallelize independent tasks; coordinate dependencies through the orchestrator.
4. **Implementation review loop:** A read-only reviewer reports actionable findings with file locations, reproduction evidence where possible, and whether each finding blocks acceptance. Route findings to the responsible implementer, apply fixes, run relevant checks, and re-review the affected behavior. Repeat for unresolved blockers; keep optional improvements deferred unless needed for the agreed scope. If a blocker cannot be resolved, report it explicitly rather than declaring completion.
5. **Integration and completion:** The orchestrator verifies the integrated user flow against the acceptance criteria. Stop when those criteria are met, required checks pass, and no blocking findings remain. Agent agreement alone is not evidence of correctness. Record unresolved limitations and verification gaps in the handoff.

Keep review rounds focused on changed behavior and outstanding findings. No commits, pushes or deployment unless requested.

## Definition of done
Working image/PDF upload and source preview, question/answer flow, explicit insufficient/unclear states, visible citations, bounded provider calls, credential-safe errors, useful tests, documented setup and limitations. Live provider claims require a successful live run; otherwise clearly report unverified integration.
# Lean 3D extension — reviewed implementation plan

Current drawing reconstruction is specified in [RECONSTRUCTION_V2_PLAN.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V2_PLAN.md) and [RECONSTRUCTION_V2_CONTRACT.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V2_CONTRACT.md). These supersede historical single-floor/relative-only restrictions; core evidence and provider invariants remain.

User-authorized scope supersedes the earlier no-3D constraint. Keep the existing local Python/plain-JS app and evidence gate. Add a browser Three.js viewer, native IFC import, then one-page approximate image reconstruction. No remote rendering, Blender, cloud, DXF/SVG/DWG, photorealism or inferred multiple storeys.

## Deliver in this order

1. Import and display one actual IFC (`ifc_bench/duplex_arc.ifc` is the first candidate). Read model geometry and properties with IfcOpenShell; preserve GlobalIds.
2. Answer explicit English whole-model IFC element-count questions through strict pattern matching + deterministic selection + the existing gate. Highlight selected elements, fade others to 0.1 opacity, click through to IFC source facts. No extra intent-model call or storey filters.
3. Generate an approximate single-floor scene from one selected image/PDF page. Store it once; reuse it across questions. Every object links to a region of the original page. Mark missing scale and assumed dimensions.
4. Connect existing image answers only where their evidence maps to scene objects reliably. Unmapped answers continue to show source-region evidence with no invented selection.

## Shared scene contract (root owns final Pydantic types)

`Scene {version:1, document_id, source_kind:"ifc"|"image", units:"m"|"relative", up_axis:"z", source_page:int|null, elements:SceneElement[], warnings:string[], catalog_complete:bool}`.

`SceneElement {id, kind:"room"|"wall"|"door"|"window"|"other", name, ifc_type:string|null, storey_id:string|null, source:SourceRef, properties:Property[], assumptions:Assumption[], geometry:Geometry|null}`.

- `SourceRef` is a tagged union: `{kind:"ifc",global_id,step_id}` or `{kind:"image",page,bbox:[left,top,right,bottom]}`. IFC facts are evidence from the supplied model, not evidence that it matches the built building. Source references never point to generated renders.
- `Property {name,value,unit:string|null,origin:"source"|"derived"}`. Keep only useful bounded primitive fields (IFC class/name/storey, supplied dimensions and selected quantities/property sets); preserve original names/units. Don't promote raw IFC lengths to metres without unit conversion or multiply already metre-based mesh coordinates again.
- `Assumption {property,value,unit,reason}` records invented dimensions separately. Source geometry and inferred image geometry must not share a blanket "verified" label. Image horizontal locations are model interpretations linked to pixels; vertical dimensions are explicit assumptions.
- `Geometry` is a small tagged union: `mesh {positions:number[],indices:int[]}`, `box {center:[x,y,z],size:[x,y,z],rotation_z:number}`, or `floor {polygon:[[x,y],...],elevation:number}`. Fixed-size arrays may need lists with length validators for SDK structured-output compatibility. All coordinates must be finite; indices in range; dimensions positive; polygon vertex counts bounded.
- IFC element IDs are the unchanged GlobalId; metadata includes STEP IDs. Reject duplicate/missing GlobalIds on selectable relevant elements rather than inventing identity. Image IDs are assigned by server in a document/page namespace and retained with the cached scene.
- Keep elements with source metadata but failed/missing geometry as `geometry:null` plus warnings. Deterministic counts operate on the complete catalog, never only on meshes. Highlighting such IDs shows their source record even if no object can be rendered.

Server uses IFC world-coordinate geometry in metres with Z-up, matching the viewer camera up vector. Image reconstruction uses relative coordinates with a fixed documented image-to-ground mapping; do not label relative scene dimensions as metres. Centering/zoom is a viewer transform and must not change source dimensions.

## Minimal API additions

- Existing upload accepts `.ifc` (actual parsed content, not extension alone). Document metadata gains `kind:"drawing"|"ifc"`; IFC has `pages:[]` and a ready scene. Existing drawing responses remain compatible. Root chooses a separate bounded IFC upload allowance (suggest 25 MiB); retain drawing limits.
- `GET /api/documents/{id}/scene`: cached scene; 404 if none has been generated.
- `POST /api/documents/{id}/scene` with `{page:1}`: one reconstruction request for a selected drawing page; returns cached result on repeat. IFC never calls a model to regenerate imported geometry. Only one selected page scene per document in this slice; do not silently replace it.
- Answers gain `highlight_ids:string[]` (default empty) and `model_evidence` for native IFC facts, while existing image `evidence` remains unchanged. Unknown floors normalize their largest panel extent to 10 display units for visibility. This is our visualization convention, not a measured length. All project coordinates are declared UNSCALED_DISPLAY_UNIT (IfcContextDependentUnit LENGTHUNIT) whenever any floor lacks calibration. Only all-calibrated projects use metres, and display-only heights/thicknesses still carry assumptions. Mixed-scale floor comparisons are not physical measurements. Per-floor calibration, transforms, orientation/order evidence and layout assumptions persist in the manifest.

## Building description
Schema source of truth is app/building.py: BuildingDescription(floors,limitations), FloorDescription(label,source,order,order_basis,rotation_degrees,orientation_basis,calibration,alignment,measurements,rooms,openings). PageRegion(page,bbox). Rooms carry label, polygon in original coordinates, basis observed|inferred, note. Openings carry kind door|window, label, original segment, source region, host_room (1-based), host_edge (0-based), basis and note. Invalid/ambiguous hosts are omitted with warnings, never attached arbitrarily. Measurements explicitly record observed/unknown, value/unit when present and source region; calibration uses a cited physical length and original segment. Alignment uses a cited source anchor and shared group; no inferred registration from matching outlines alone.

On the model wire points use named `x`/`y` fields and regions named `left`/`top`/`right`/`bottom`; internal canonical coordinates remain arrays. Gemini reconstruction uses medium reasoning following a controlled live quality comparison; existing response budgets and answer/gate settings remain unchanged.

Process ALL uploaded source pages, including multiple diagram regions per page. No new floor/room/vertex count caps: remove old extraction30/40 limits. Retain original upload10MiB/5pages/40MP/4096edge and IFC25MiB/4000elements/1milliontriangles safeguards. These can reject large inputs and artifact expansion from embedded source PNGs; no silent truncation. The existing answer100citations/4000highlights and generation token budget bound responses, not model coverage. Explain output incompleteness rather than deriving factual counts from generated inventory.

Strict finite coordinates, page bounds, valid polygons and nonzero dimensions are necessary geometry checks, not sampling limits. Per-floor invalid geometry is omitted transparently; overlapping-room conflicts are detected before filtering. Separate-floor polygons may overlap on different pages without conflict. Preserve a floor record even if no room survives, with a warning; reject only if the entire building has no renderable rooms.

## Identity, persistence and trust
Generate artifact namespace once from originating document.id; persist it as artifact_id. UUID5/artifact namespace + stable floor/room/opening indices produces compressed IFC GlobalIds. Keep those IDs on reopening under a fresh document.id. Stable indices survive partial omission.

Generator owns app/ifc_generate.py only: generate_ifc(description, document) -> bytes. It constructs IFC4 using IfcOpenShell entities, project/building/storeys/spaces/walls/opening voids/fills. Embed a versioned manifest under Pset_BlueprintQA on IfcProject plus per-element provenance. Source page PNGs, hashes and dimensions are embedded in the manifest; scene metadata, source references, observations and assumptions survive. No runtime network paths or filesystem paths in the artifact. Source images are the exact normalized original previews, never renders.

Root owns app/ifc_artifact.py: recognize generated markers BEFORE native catalog construction; validate version, source hashes/PNG bounds, source refs, manifest and IFC identity; restore pages and scene provenance, then tessellate actual IFC geometry. Recognizable own markers with missing/inconsistent provenance reject; no fallback to native IFC. Detection includes own project marker/property set or UNSCALED_DISPLAY_UNIT. Fully stripped/forged metadata cannot authenticate arbitrary third-party IFC; do not claim it can.

Both direct import_ifc and DocumentStore route recognized derived artifacts through the derived importer. Freshly uploaded generated IFC becomes document.kind=drawing with restored original pages and scene.source_kind=image, derived=true, catalog_complete=false, geometry_origin=inferred. It MUST NOT enter native deterministic count or property-evidence paths. Generated properties, dimensions and floor inventories are association hints only. QA receives original source pixels; it never receives embedded IFC quantities as factual evidence.

## Scene / UI / API
Extend Scene with derived:bool, artifact_id, floors:list[SceneFloor], ifc_url, layout. SceneFloor fields: id,label,source,order,scale_status,rotation_degrees,alignment_status,observations,assumptions. SceneElement gains evidence_basis and note; storey_id is its floor GlobalId. Scene.units remains relative|m but badges also inspect derived and per-floor scale. Generated room meshes are floor plates and visible by default; native enclosed space volumes retain their existing behavior.

POST /api/documents/{id}/scene generates the whole document; legacy page argument may be accepted but cannot restrict extraction. Cache once. GET /api/documents/{id}/model.ifc downloads cached bytes. Public document/scene exposes download URL. Reopened artifacts expose both original pages and the same IFC download.

Viewer adds floor filter, source-linked floor labels and independent exploded display toggle, plus derived IFC download. Multifloor schematic derived scenes default to separated display. Highlighting/assumptions remain separate. Evidence on a hidden floor reveals it. Source clicks use original page/bbox even after rotation, layout, export and reopening. Image highlight validation uses the correct source page/region and exact normalized label, never generated dimensions; uncertain mapping keeps evidence and leaves highlights empty.

## What the AI SDK Is

The AI SDK by Vercel (the `ai` package on npm) is a TypeScript toolkit for building AI applications. It provides a unified API across model providers for text generation, structured output, tool calling, agents, embeddings, and framework UI integrations.

- Repository: https://github.com/vercel/ai
- Documentation: https://ai-sdk.dev/docs

## Critical: Do Not Trust Your Own Memory

Whatever you remember about the AI SDK is likely outdated. The SDK changes frequently across versions - APIs are renamed, removed, and added. Your training data almost certainly contains obsolete APIs, deprecated patterns, and model IDs that no longer exist. UI hooks like `useChat` are among the most frequently changed APIs, so be especially careful with client code.

**Never write AI SDK code from memory.** Always verify every API, option, and pattern against the documentation and source code for the version that is actually installed in the project.

## Use the Bundled, Version-Matched Docs

The `ai` package ships its full documentation and source code inside `node_modules`. These always match the installed version, so trust them over anything you remember.

1. Ensure `ai` is installed. Check `node_modules/ai/` or locate the workspace package in a monorepo that depends on `ai` (e.g. `apps/<name>/node_modules/ai/`). If `ai` is not installed anywhere in the project, install **only** the `ai` package into the target package using the project's package manager (e.g. `pnpm add ai --filter <pkg>` or `npm install ai`). Install provider packages (e.g. `@ai-sdk/openai`) and framework packages (e.g. `@ai-sdk/react`) later, when the task requires them.
2. Read and grep the bundled docs at `node_modules/ai/docs/` (or `<package>/node_modules/ai/docs/`) and the source at `node_modules/ai/src/`.
3. Provider and framework packages bundle their own docs at `node_modules/@ai-sdk/<name>/docs/` (or `<package>/node_modules/@ai-sdk/<name>/docs/`).
4. If something isn't in the bundled docs, search https://ai-sdk.dev/docs. You can append `.md` to any docs page URL to get its markdown, and search via `https://ai-sdk.dev/api/search-docs?q=your_query`.
5. If you cannot find support for an answer in the docs or source, say so explicitly — do not guess.

## AI Gateway: The Fastest Way to Start

The Vercel AI Gateway is the fastest way to get started with the AI SDK. It provides access to models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and other providers through a single API, without installing provider packages or managing multiple API keys.

To set it up:

1. Authenticate with OIDC (for Vercel deployments) or get an AI Gateway API key.
2. Provide it to your app via the `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` environment variable.
3. Reference models with `provider/model` strings.

For exact setup, authentication, and usage, read the bundled guide and the AI Gateway docs.

### Choosing a Model

Never use model IDs from memory — models are released and retired frequently. Fetch the current list before writing code that references a model. Do not truncate the list (e.g. with `head`) so you can find the newest models:

```bash
# All available models
curl -s https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models | jq -r '.data[].id'

# Filter by provider (e.g. anthropic, openai, google)
curl -s https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models | jq -r '[.data[] | select(.id | startswith("anthropic/")) | .id] | reverse | .[]'
```

When multiple versions of a model exist, prefer the one with the highest version number.

## Building and Consuming Agents

Use the SDK's built-in agent abstraction (such as `ToolLoopAgent`) rather than hand-rolling tool-calling loops. For end-to-end type safety, infer the UI message type from your agent definition when consuming it on the client (e.g. with `useChat`). Consuming an agent is framework-specific: check `package.json` to detect the stack, then follow the matching quickstart.

Look up the current agent, tool, and type-safety APIs in the bundled docs (`node_modules/ai/docs/`, especially the agents section) or at https://ai-sdk.dev/docs.

## DevTools

AI SDK DevTools captures your AI SDK calls - requests, responses, tool calls, token usage, and multi-step runs - so you can inspect exactly what your agents do. Use it while developing to debug generations. It is a separate package and is intended for local development only.

For setup instructions, read the bundled DevTools documentation.

## Keep the SDK Current

Outdated installs are the most common source of errors. Compare the installed version against the latest:

- **Installed:** the `version` field in `node_modules/ai/package.json`.
- **Latest:** run `npm view ai version`.

If the installed version is a major version (or more) behind the latest, tell the user they are on an old release, and recommend upgrading before continuing. Migration guides are at https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/migration-guides.

## After Making Changes

Run the project's type checker. Be minimal — only set options that differ from the defaults, checking docs or source for the defaults rather than over-specifying. Most type errors come from remembered, now-changed APIs; re-check the current docs and source when they occur.

## What the AI SDK Is

The AI SDK by Vercel (the `ai` package on npm) is a TypeScript toolkit for building AI applications. It provides a unified API across model providers for text generation, structured output, tool calling, agents, embeddings, and framework UI integrations.

- Repository: https://github.com/vercel/ai
- Documentation: https://ai-sdk.dev/docs

## Critical: Do Not Trust Your Own Memory

Whatever you remember about the AI SDK is likely outdated. The SDK changes frequently across versions - APIs are renamed, removed, and added. Your training data almost certainly contains obsolete APIs, deprecated patterns, and model IDs that no longer exist. UI hooks like `useChat` are among the most frequently changed APIs, so be especially careful with client code.

**Never write AI SDK code from memory.** Always verify every API, option, and pattern against the documentation and source code for the version that is actually installed in the project.

## Use the Bundled, Version-Matched Docs

The `ai` package ships its full documentation and source code inside `node_modules`. These always match the installed version, so trust them over anything you remember.

1. Ensure `ai` is installed. Check `node_modules/ai/` or locate the workspace package in a monorepo that depends on `ai` (e.g. `apps/<name>/node_modules/ai/`). If `ai` is not installed anywhere in the project, install **only** the `ai` package into the target package using the project's package manager (e.g. `pnpm add ai --filter <pkg>` or `npm install ai`). Install provider packages (e.g. `@ai-sdk/openai`) and framework packages (e.g. `@ai-sdk/react`) later, when the task requires them.
2. Read and grep the bundled docs at `node_modules/ai/docs/` (or `<package>/node_modules/ai/docs/`) and the source at `node_modules/ai/src/`.
3. Provider and framework packages bundle their own docs at `node_modules/@ai-sdk/<name>/docs/` (or `<package>/node_modules/@ai-sdk/<name>/docs/`).
4. If something isn't in the bundled docs, search https://ai-sdk.dev/docs. You can append `.md` to any docs page URL to get its markdown, and search via `https://ai-sdk.dev/api/search-docs?q=your_query`.
5. If you cannot find support for an answer in the docs or source, say so explicitly — do not guess.

## AI Gateway: The Fastest Way to Start

The Vercel AI Gateway is the fastest way to get started with the AI SDK. It provides access to models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and other providers through a single API, without installing provider packages or managing multiple API keys.

To set it up:

1. Authenticate with OIDC (for Vercel deployments) or get an AI Gateway API key.
2. Provide it to your app via the `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` environment variable.
3. Reference models with `provider/model` strings.

For exact setup, authentication, and usage, read the bundled guide and the AI Gateway docs.

### Choosing a Model

Never use model IDs from memory — models are released and retired frequently. Fetch the current list before writing code that references a model. Do not truncate the list (e.g. with `head`) so you can find the newest models:

```bash
# All available models
curl -s https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models | jq -r '.data[].id'

# Filter by provider (e.g. anthropic, openai, google)
curl -s https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models | jq -r '[.data[] | select(.id | startswith("anthropic/")) | .id] | reverse | .[]'
```

When multiple versions of a model exist, prefer the one with the highest version number.

## Building and Consuming Agents

Use the SDK's built-in agent abstraction (such as `ToolLoopAgent`) rather than hand-rolling tool-calling loops. For end-to-end type safety, infer the UI message type from your agent definition when consuming it on the client (e.g. with `useChat`). Consuming an agent is framework-specific: check `package.json` to detect the stack, then follow the matching quickstart.

Look up the current agent, tool, and type-safety APIs in the bundled docs (`node_modules/ai/docs/`, especially the agents section) or at https://ai-sdk.dev/docs.

## DevTools

AI SDK DevTools captures your AI SDK calls - requests, responses, tool calls, token usage, and multi-step runs - so you can inspect exactly what your agents do. Use it while developing to debug generations. It is a separate package and is intended for local development only.

For setup instructions, read the bundled DevTools documentation.

## Keep the SDK Current

Outdated installs are the most common source of errors. Compare the installed version against the latest:

- **Installed:** the `version` field in `node_modules/ai/package.json`.
- **Latest:** run `npm view ai version`.

If the installed version is a major version (or more) behind the latest, tell the user they are on an old release, and recommend upgrading before continuing. Migration guides are at https://ai-sdk.dev/docs/migration-guides.

## After Making Changes

Run the project's type checker. Be minimal — only set options that differ from the defaults, checking docs or source for the defaults rather than over-specifying. Most type errors come from remembered, now-changed APIs; re-check the current docs and source when they occur.

from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from pathlib import Path
import threading

from fastapi import FastAPI, File, HTTPException, UploadFile
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse, Response
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
from starlette.concurrency import run_in_threadpool

from .documents import DocumentError, DocumentStore, MAX_UPLOAD, MAX_IFC_UPLOAD
from .scene import Scene
from .schemas import StrictModel
from pydantic import Field
from .provider import create_provider, ProviderError, settings
from .schemas import Answer, AskRequest
from .service import ask

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


class SceneRequest(StrictModel):
    page: int = Field(default=1, ge=1, le=5)


def create_app(*, provider_factory=create_provider, storage_root=None):
    @asynccontextmanager
    async def lifespan(application):
        application.state.documents = DocumentStore(Path(storage_root or ROOT / ".runtime"))
        yield
        application.state.documents.close()

    application = FastAPI(title="Blueprint QA", lifespan=lifespan)
    application.state.provider_factory = provider_factory
    application.state.inference_slots = threading.BoundedSemaphore(2)
    application.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory=ROOT / "app" / "static", check_dir=False), name="static")

    @application.get("/")
    def index():
        return FileResponse(ROOT / "app" / "static" / "index.html")

    @application.get("/api/health")
    def health():
        try:
            config = settings()
        except ProviderError as error:
            raise HTTPException(error.status, error.message) from None
        return {"status": "ok", "provider_ready": bool(config["api_key"]), "model": config["model"],
                "provider": config["name"], "provider_label": config["label"],
                "credential_env": config["credential_env"], "gate_kind": config["gate_kind"],
                "decision_model": config["decision_model"], "limits": {"max_upload_mb": 10, "max_ifc_mb": 25, "max_pages": 5}}

    @application.post("/api/documents")
    async def upload(file: UploadFile = File(...)):
        try:
            data = await file.read(MAX_IFC_UPLOAD + 1)
            document = await run_in_threadpool(application.state.documents.add, data, file.filename or "Untitled plan")
            return document.public()
        except DocumentError as error:
            raise HTTPException(error.status, error.message) from None
        finally:
            await file.close()

    @application.get("/api/documents/{document_id}/pages/{page}")
    def preview(document_id: str, page: int):
        try:
            document = application.state.documents.get(document_id)
            if not 1 <= page <= len(document.pages):
                raise DocumentError("Page not found.", 404)
            return FileResponse(document.pages[page - 1].path, media_type="image/png", headers={"Cache-Control": "no-store"})
        except DocumentError as error:
            raise HTTPException(error.status, error.message) from None

    @application.post("/api/ask", response_model=Answer)
    def question(request: AskRequest):
        provider = None
        if not application.state.inference_slots.acquire(blocking=False):
            raise HTTPException(429, "Two questions are already processing. Please wait and retry.")
        try:
            document = application.state.documents.get(request.document_id)
            provider = application.state.provider_factory()
            return ask(document, request.question, provider)
        except (DocumentError, ProviderError) as error:
            raise HTTPException(error.status, error.message) from None
        finally:
            application.state.inference_slots.release()
            if provider is not None:
                provider.close()

    @application.get("/api/documents/{document_id}/scene", response_model=Scene)
    def get_scene(document_id: str):
        try:
            document = application.state.documents.get(document_id)
            if not document.scene:
                raise DocumentError("No model yet. Generate a building model from the original drawing pages.", 404)
            return document.scene
        except DocumentError as error:
            raise HTTPException(error.status, error.message) from None

    @application.post("/api/documents/{document_id}/scene", response_model=Scene)
    def generate_scene(document_id: str, request: SceneRequest):
        provider = None
        acquired = False
        try:
            document = application.state.documents.get(document_id)
            with document.scene_lock:
                if document.scene:
                    return document.scene
                if not 1 <= request.page <= len(document.pages):
                    raise DocumentError("Page not found.", 404)
                acquired = application.state.inference_slots.acquire(blocking=False)
                if not acquired:
                    raise DocumentError("Two model requests are already processing. Please retry shortly.", 429)
                from .reconstruction import reconstruct_scene
                provider = application.state.provider_factory()
                scene = reconstruct_scene(document, request.page, provider)
                document.scene = scene
                return scene
        except (DocumentError, ProviderError) as error:
            raise HTTPException(error.status, error.message) from None
        finally:
            if acquired:
                application.state.inference_slots.release()
            if provider:
                provider.close()

    @application.get("/api/documents/{document_id}/model.ifc")
    def download_model(document_id: str):
        try:
            document = application.state.documents.get(document_id)
            if not document.ifc_bytes:
                raise DocumentError("Generate the drawing-derived IFC first.", 404)
            return Response(document.ifc_bytes, media_type="application/x-step",
                            headers={"Content-Disposition": 'attachment; filename="blueprint-derived.ifc"',
                                     "Cache-Control": "no-store"})
        except DocumentError as error:
            raise HTTPException(error.status, error.message) from None

    return application


app = create_app()

class ProviderError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, message: str, status: int = 502):
        self.message, self.status = message, status


def gemini_wire_schema(schema: dict) -> dict:
    """Relax array upper bounds only on Gemini's wire; validate the full model locally.

    The current endpoint rejects these bounds for our reconstruction schema. Walk
    schema locations, not arbitrary JSON values: a property named ``maxItems``
    or an object inside a default/enum remains ordinary data.
    """
    result = deepcopy(schema)

    def visit(node):
        if not isinstance(node, dict):
            return
        kind = node.get("type")
        if kind == "array" or isinstance(kind, list) and "array" in kind:
            node.pop("maxItems", None)
        for keyword in ("$defs", "definitions", "properties", "patternProperties", "dependentSchemas"):
            for child in node.get(keyword, {}).values():
                visit(child)
        for keyword in ("anyOf", "allOf", "oneOf", "prefixItems"):
            for child in node.get(keyword, []):
                visit(child)
        for keyword in ("items", "additionalProperties", "contains", "not", "if", "then", "else",
                        "propertyNames", "unevaluatedProperties", "unevaluatedItems"):
            visit(node.get(keyword))

    visit(result)
    return result


def settings(provider_name=None):
    name = (provider_name or os.getenv("AI_PROVIDER", "gemini")).strip().lower()
    if name not in {"gemini", "openai"}:
        raise ProviderError("Unknown AI_PROVIDER. Choose gemini or openai and restart the server.", 503)
    if name == "openai":
        model = os.getenv("OPENAI_MODEL", "gpt-6.1-sol")
        return {"name": name, "label": "OpenAI", "credential_env": "OPENAI_API_KEY",
                "api_key": os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY", "").strip(), "model": model,
                "decision_model": model, "gate_kind": "structured_classification"}
    return {
        "name": name, "label": "Gemini", "credential_env": "GEMINI_API_KEY",
        "gate_kind": "gemini_decisions",
        "api_key": os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY", "").strip(),
        "model": os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL", "gemini-3.8-flash"),
        "decision_model": os.getenv("GEMINI_DECISION_MODEL", "gemini-decision-1"),
    }


def create_provider():
    if settings()["name"] == "openai":
        from .openai_provider import OpenAIProvider
        return OpenAIProvider()
    return GeminiProvider()


def image_bytes(image, edge=1600):
    image = image.copy()
    image.thumbnail((edge, edge))
    output = BytesIO()
    image.save(output, format="PNG")
    image.close()
    return output.getvalue()


def views(document: Document, crop: CropRequest | None = None):
    """All source pages, plus at most one true crop from stored source pixels."""
    result = []
    for page in document.pages:
        with page.image() as image:
            result.append((f"Original source page {page.number}. Coordinates refer to this whole page.", image_bytes(image)))
    if crop:
        page = document.pages[crop.page - 1]
        with page.image() as image:
            left, top, right, bottom = crop.bbox
            region = image.crop((int(left * image.width), int(top * image.height),
                                 max(int(right * image.width), int(left * image.width) + 1),
                                 max(int(bottom * image.height), int(top * image.height) + 1)))
            try:
                result.append((f"Detail crop of original page {crop.page}, normalized bounds {list(crop.bbox)}. "
                               "This is the SAME source, not a separate object or page. Cite original-page coordinates.",
                               image_bytes(region, edge=2400)))
            finally:
                region.close()
    return result

"""

def normalize(image: Image.Image) -> Image.Image:
    if image.width * image.height > MAX_PIXELS:
        raise DocumentError("Image exceeds the 40 megapixel limit.", 413)
    image = ImageOps.exif_transpose(image)
    if image.mode in ("RGBA", "LA") or "transparency" in image.info:
        rgba = image.convert("RGBA")
        result = Image.new("RGB", image.size, "white")
        result.paste(rgba, mask=rgba.getchannel("A"))
    else:
        result = image.convert("RGB")
    result.thumbnail((MAX_EDGE, MAX_EDGE))
    return result

p.write_text('''# Voice interaction contract

Root owns this integration contract. Voice input/output augment the existing source-grounded question flow; they do not establish building facts.

## Endpoints

- `GET /api/voice/config`: `{transcription_ready,speech_ready,transcription_model,language_codes}`. Readiness means configuration is present, not successful provider access. Voice transcription uses Gemini independently of the selected QA provider.
- `GET /api/documents/{id}/voice-vocabulary`: `{terms:[str],rooms:[{id,name,floor_label}],warnings:[str]}`. Names come from cached room elements including geometry-less IFC records, plus floor names. Native floors can come from `Storey.Name`. Drawing names are fallible recognition hints and become available after reconstruction or generated-IFC reopening; no extra extraction request is made. Custom terms work before a scene exists. No generated dimensions or assumptions enter recognition or factual answering.
- WebSocket `/api/voice/transcribe`: initial JSON `{type:"start",document_id,custom_vocabulary:[str]}`. Server deduplicates building/custom vocabulary, validates document and configuration, opens Google, and emits `{type:"ready"}`. Client then streams signed little-endian PCM16 mono at 16 kHz as binary messages. AudioWorklet converts the actual browser sample rate. Server emits `{type:"transcript",text,final:boolean}`; finals append and interim text replaces the previous interim. Client `{type:"stop"}` flushes audio and waits for finalization; `{type:"cancel"}` or disconnect aborts. Successful completion emits `{type:"done"}`. Operational failures emit `{type:"error",message}` with safe text and preserve already received transcript text. Never treat a timeout as successful finalization.
- `POST /api/voice/speech`: `{document_id,text}` -> `audio/mpeg`, no-store. UI sends the exact displayed answer, including insufficient/unclear wording. No summarizer or new factual inference. Unknown documents return 404, missing configuration 503, upstream failures 502. Full MP3 is fetched before playback.

## Aliases and evidence

Aliases are user-defined, per-document browser-memory mappings to a selected room. Exact Unicode-boundary matching is case-insensitive, longest-first and nonrecursive. The UI shows the recognized text and editable canonical replacement before explicit Ask. Duplicate room names require floor qualification; duplicated name+floor targets are ambiguous and cannot receive an ID-specific alias through the text-only question API. Aliases and custom terms are hints, never evidence. The existing question endpoint, sufficiency gate, source citations and highlight validation remain authoritative.

## Lifecycle and limits

Only a user action opens the microphone. Recording and playback exclude one another. Stop, cancel, document replacement, new questions and page departure release microphone tracks, audio processing, sockets, pending synthesis and playback resources as appropriate. Delayed callbacks from an older recording/document cannot modify the current question or answer. Browser playback restrictions expose a manual playback fallback. Voice failures preserve ordinary text input, answers and citations.

Google documents at most 1,000 custom-vocabulary phrases; excess combined hints are explicitly rejected rather than truncated. There is no additional recording-duration or room-count cap. Configurable connection/finalization/synthesis deadlines release stalled operations; a finalization deadline reports incomplete transcription. Speech is limited to 6,000 characters, matching the original draft-answer bound; an expanded final answer may exceed that and remains text-only with a clear error, never silent truncation. Provider cancellation cannot reverse already billed work.

## Provider references

Verified 2026-11-14 against current documentation and installed google-genai 3.3.0:
- https://aistudio.google.com/docs/live-api/live-transcribe — Gemini Live transcription and custom vocabulary.
- https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-speech/convert — ElevenLabs text-to-speech MP3 conversion.

Factories are injected for deterministic tests; fixture transcription and speech must never be described as live inference. Recognition improvement requires paired recordings with/without hints; configuration acceptance alone is insufficient.
''')

No credentials, uploads or dataset files were copied into it.

Configure `.env.local` in this worktree using the placeholders in `.env.example`:

- `GEMINI_API_KEY`: Google key for live transcription (also used for Gemini QA).
- `GEMINI_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL=gemini-3.5-transcribe-live`.
- `VOICE_LANGUAGE_CODES=`: empty for automatic language detection; optional comma-separated language codes such as `en-US,fi-FI`.

- `ELEVENLABS_MODEL_ID=eleven_multilingual_v2`.

Readiness means configuration exists, not that provider access is verified. Diagnose with `.venv/bin/python scripts/doctor.py`, run with `bash scripts/dev.sh`. Microphone capture needs localhost or HTTPS and browser microphone permission.

## Use

1. Upload a plan/PDF/IFC. Native IFC names are available immediately. Drawings gain automatic hints after Generate Model; reopened generated IFC restores those hints.
2. Add custom words if needed. Names interpreted from drawings are fallible and remain recognition hints.
3. Add an easier alias by selecting its room. Floor-qualified names distinguish repeated room names. A duplicated name on the same floor requires explicit clarification instead of an ambiguous alias. Aliases/terms last only for this document in the current page session.
4. Record, speak, and Stop. Review the recognized words and any alias replacement, edit the question, and press Ask. Recording never submits a question automatically.
5. Read the answer aloud or enable automatic reading. Stop cancels pending synthesis/playback. Text, citations and highlights remain available if speech fails.

## Boundaries

Hints influence recognition without guaranteeing it. Google documents at most 1,000 combined phrases; excess hints produce an explicit error. No extra provider call extracts labels solely for voice. Rooms omitted by reconstruction are absent from automatic hints and can be added manually.

Browser autoplay restrictions may require manual playback.

Stopping recording waits for Google's manual turn completion. Timeout or interrupted finalization preserves received text with an error; review before submission. Starting another interaction invalidates stale callbacks. Cancelling a provider request does not undo any usage already incurred. Audio is forwarded during the active session and is not persisted by this app. Provider retention follows the provider/account settings.

## Verification

Implementation verification is recorded in the branch handoff after integrated testing. Deterministic fixtures are explicitly injected and are not evidence of live recognition or speech quality. result.output:
turn_complete: If true, indicates that the model is done generating. Generation will only start in response to additional client messages. Can be set alongside `content`, indicating that the `content` is the last in the turn.
generation_complete: If true, indicates that the model is done generating. When model is
      interrupted while generating there will be no generation_complete message
      in interrupted turn, it will go through interrupted > turn_complete.
      When model assumes realtime playback there will be delay between
      generation_complete and turn_complete that is caused by model
      waiting for playback to finish. If true, indicates that the model
      has finished generating all content. This is a signal to the client
      that it can stop sending messages.
input_transcription: Input transcription. The transcription is independent to the model
      turn which means it doesn’t imply any ordering between transcription and
      model turn.
interaction_status: The current activity status of the live session. Always sent alongside `turn_complete`.

---
name: text-to-speech
description: Convert text to speech using ElevenLabs voice AI. Use when generating audio from text, creating voiceovers, building voice apps, or synthesizing speech in 90+ languages.
license: MIT
compatibility: Requires internet access and an ElevenLabs API key (ELEVENLABS_API_KEY).
metadata: {"openclaw": {"requires": {"env": ["ELEVENLABS_API_KEY"]}, "primaryEnv": "ELEVENLABS_API_KEY"}}
---

# ElevenLabs Text-to-Speech

Generate natural speech from text - supports 90+ languages, multiple models for quality vs latency tradeoffs. Examples default to `eleven_v4`, the latest and highest-quality model.

> **Setup, before writing any code:** if `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` isn't set for this project, run `npx -y @elevenlabs/cli@latest onboard init` from the app's folder first and follow what it prints: it signs the user in and stores a key for the project, so nobody copies one by hand. Otherwise see the [Installation Guide](references/installation.md). For JavaScript, use `@elevenlabs/*` packages only.

## Quick Start

### Python

```python
from elevenlabs import ElevenLabs

client = ElevenLabs()

audio = client.text_to_speech.convert(
    text="Hello, welcome to ElevenLabs!",
    voice_id="JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb",  # George
    model_id="eleven_v4"
)

with open("output.mp3", "wb") as f:
    for chunk in audio:
        f.write(chunk)
```

### JavaScript

```javascript
import { ElevenLabsClient } from "@elevenlabs/elevenlabs-js";
import { createWriteStream } from "fs";
import { Readable } from "stream";

const client = new ElevenLabsClient();
const audio = await client.textToSpeech.convert("JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb", {
  text: "Hello, welcome to ElevenLabs!",
  modelId: "eleven_v4",
});
// convert() returns a web ReadableStream — bridge it to a Node stream to write to disk
Readable.fromWeb(audio).pipe(createWriteStream("output.mp3"));
```

### CLI

Use `say` to play text immediately with the default voice and `eleven_v3` model:

```bash
elevenlabs say "Hello!"
```

Pipe text into `say` when another command produces the input:

```bash
echo "The build finished successfully." | elevenlabs say
```

Use the API command when you need to set request parameters directly:

```bash
elevenlabs text-to-speech convert --voice-id JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb \
  --text "Hello!" --model-id eleven_v4 --output output.mp3
```

The CLI reads `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` from the environment automatically.

## Models

| Model ID | Languages | Latency | Best For |
|----------|-----------|---------|----------|
| `eleven_v4` | 90+ | Standard | **Default.** Highest quality, emotional range, audio tags, voice cloning accuracy |
| `eleven_v4_turbo` | 90+ | ~100ms | Real-time v4 quality for agents and interactive apps (via [Text to Dialogue WebSocket](references/streaming.md#eleven-v4-turbo-websocket)) |
| `eleven_flash_v2_5` | 32 | ~75ms | Lowest latency, lowest cost, `stream-input` WebSocket |
| `eleven_flash_v2` | English | ~75ms | English-only, lowest latency |
| `eleven_multilingual_v2` | 29 | Standard | Previous generation; most stable on very long-form generations |
| `eleven_v3` | 70+ | Standard | Previous generation expressive model |

`eleven_turbo_v2_5` and `eleven_turbo_v2` are superseded by the Flash models (same output, lower latency) — use `eleven_flash_v2_5` / `eleven_flash_v2` instead.

**Eleven v4 notes:** supports only `stability` and `similarity_boost` voice settings (no `style` or `speed`), does not support SSML, and is not available on the `stream-input` TTS WebSocket. Direct delivery with audio tags such as `[whispers]`, `[laughs]`, `[sarcastic]`.

## Voice IDs

Use pre-made voices or create custom voices in the dashboard.

**Popular voices:**
- `JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb` - George (male, narrative)
- `EXAVITQu4vr4xnSDxMaL` - Sarah (female, soft)
- `onwK4e9ZLuTAKqWW03F9` - Daniel (male, authoritative)

**Pick a voice the account's plan can use.** Free plans can use pre-made voices through the API, but not Voice Library voices: those fail with a `402` (`paid_plan_required`). Use George unless the user asks for something else. Do not use a voice ID from memory. Tutorials still use voices that have since been retired (Rachel, Charlotte, Josh and others), and those fail the same way on a free plan. To choose another voice, list the pre-made ones:

```python
voices = client.voices.get_all()
for voice in voices.voices:
    if voice.category == "premade":
        print(f"{voice.voice_id}: {voice.name}")
```

## Voice Settings

Fine-tune how the voice sounds:

- **Stability**: How consistent the voice stays. Lower values = more emotional range and variation, but can sound unstable. Higher = steady, predictable delivery.
- **Similarity boost**: How closely to match the original voice sample. Higher values sound more like the original but may amplify audio artifacts.
- **Style**: Exaggerates the voice's unique style characteristics (v2/v3 models; not supported on Eleven v4).
- **Speed**: Speech speed multiplier (v2/v3 models; not supported on Eleven v4).
- **Speaker boost**: Post-processing that enhances clarity and voice similarity.

```python
from elevenlabs import VoiceSettings

audio = client.text_to_speech.convert(
    text="Customize my voice settings.",
    voice_id="JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb",
    model_id="eleven_v4",
    voice_settings=VoiceSettings(
        stability=0.5,          # Lower = more expressive, higher = more consistent
        similarity_boost=0.75,  # Higher = closer to the reference voice
    )
)
```

## Language Selection

Use `language_code` with models that support language enforcement to guide pronunciation and text normalization. Unsupported language codes are ignored, and `language_code` is not supported on `eleven_multilingual_v2`.

```python
audio = client.text_to_speech.convert(
    text="Bonjour, comment allez-vous?",
    voice_id="JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb",
    model_id="eleven_v4",
    language_code="fr"  # ISO 639-1 code
)
```

## Text Normalization

Controls how numbers, dates, and abbreviations are converted to spoken words. For example, "01/15/2026" becomes "January fifteenth, twenty twenty-six":

- `"auto"` (default): Model decides based on context
- `"on"`: Always normalize (use when you want natural speech)
- `"off"`: Speak literally (use when you want "zero one slash one five...")

```python
audio = client.text_to_speech.convert(
    text="Call 1-800-555-0123 on 01/15/2026",
    voice_id="JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb",
    model_id="eleven_v4",
    apply_text_normalization="on"
)
```

## Audio Effects

Use `audio_effects` to process the generated audio with a filter preset, perceived distance, a reverb environment, a looped background noise bed, and stereo panning. Effects do not change the cost of a request.

| Field | Range | Description |
|-------|-------|-------------|
| `filter_preset_id` | Catalog ID | Filter that colors the voice, such as `phone` or `old_radio` |
| `distance` | 0-1 (default 0) | How far the speaker sounds from the microphone |
| `environment_id` | Catalog ID | Reverb environment, such as `small_room` or `hall` |
| `send_level` | 0-1 (default 1) | How much of the voice feeds the reverb; 0 turns reverb off |
| `background_noise_id` | Catalog ID | Background noise looped under the voice, such as `cafe` or `keyboard` |
| `pan` | -1 to 1 (default 0) | Stereo position of the voice, from hard left to hard right |

List valid filter preset, environment, and background noise IDs with the catalog endpoint (`GET /v1/audio-effects/catalog`):

```python
from elevenlabs import EffectsSpecInput

catalog = client.audio_effects.get_catalog()
for environment in catalog.environments:
    print(f"{environment.environment_id}: {environment.name}")

audio = client.text_to_speech.convert(
    text="Welcome to the concert hall.",
    voice_id="JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb",
    model_id="eleven_v4",
    audio_effects=EffectsSpecInput(
        environment_id="hall",
        distance=0.3,
        pan=-0.5,
    )
)
```

Reverb and non-zero `pan` produce stereo audio and are rejected for `ulaw_*`, `alaw_*`, and `pcm_*` output formats. Unknown effect IDs return a 404 error.

## Request Stitching

When generating long audio in multiple requests, the audio can have pops, unnatural pauses, or tone shifts at the boundaries. Request stitching solves this by letting each request know what comes before/after it:

```python
# First request
audio1 = client.text_to_speech.convert(
    text="This is the first part.",
    voice_id="JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb",
    model_id="eleven_v4",
    next_text="And this continues the story."
)

# Second request using previous context
audio2 = client.text_to_speech.convert(
    text="And this continues the story.",
    voice_id="JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb",
    model_id="eleven_v4",
    previous_text="This is the first part."
)
```

## Output Formats

| Format | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `mp3_44100_128` | MP3 44.1kHz 128kbps (default) - compressed, good for web/apps |
| `mp3_44100_192` | MP3 44.1kHz 192kbps (Creator+) - higher quality compressed |
| `mp3_44100_64` | MP3 44.1kHz 64kbps - lower quality, smaller files |
| `mp3_22050_32` | MP3 22.05kHz 32kbps - smallest MP3 files |
| `pcm_16000` | Raw PCM 16kHz - use for real-time processing |
| `pcm_22050` | Raw PCM 22.05kHz |
| `pcm_24000` | Raw PCM 24kHz - good balance for streaming |
| `pcm_44100` | Raw PCM 44.1kHz (Pro+) - CD quality |
| `pcm_48000` | Raw PCM 48kHz (Pro+) - highest quality |
| `ulaw_8000` | μ-law 8kHz - standard for phone systems (Twilio, telephony) |
| `alaw_8000` | A-law 8kHz - telephony (alternative to μ-law) |
| `opus_48000_64` | Opus 48kHz 64kbps - efficient streaming codec |
| `wav_44100` | WAV 44.1kHz - uncompressed with headers |

## Streaming

Use the `stream` method to receive audio chunks as they're generated:

```python
audio_stream = client.text_to_speech.stream(
    text="This text will be streamed as audio.",
    voice_id="JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb",
    model_id="eleven_v4"
)

for chunk in audio_stream:
    play_audio(chunk)
```

For real-time apps where latency matters most, use `eleven_v4_turbo` (~100ms) over the Text to Dialogue WebSocket, or `eleven_flash_v2_5` (~75ms) over HTTP streaming or the `stream-input` WebSocket. See [references/streaming.md](references/streaming.md).

## Error Handling

```python
try:
    audio = client.text_to_speech.convert(
        text="Generate speech",
        voice_id="invalid-voice-id",
        model_id="eleven_v4"
    )
except Exception as e:
    print(f"API error: {e}")
```

Common errors:
- **401**: Invalid API key
- **422**: Invalid parameters (check voice_id, model_id)
- **429**: Rate limit exceeded

## Tracking Costs

Monitor character usage via response headers (`x-character-count`, `request-id`):

```python
response = client.text_to_speech.convert.with_raw_response(
    text="Hello!", voice_id="JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb", model_id="eleven_v4"
)
audio = response.parse()
print(f"Characters used: {response.headers.get('x-character-count')}")
```

## References

- [Installation Guide](references/installation.md)
- [Streaming Audio](references/streaming.md)
- [Voice Settings](references/voice-settings.md)

Current drawing reconstruction is specified in [RECONSTRUCTION_V2_PLAN.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V2_PLAN.md) and [RECONSTRUCTION_V2_CONTRACT.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V2_CONTRACT.md). These supersede historical single-floor/relative-only restrictions; core evidence and provider invariants remain.

Local-first single-process app. JPG/PNG and small PDFs are mandatory. FastAPI serves static UI and API. Render PDF pages with PDFium and send the rendered source images to Gemini/Decisions; always identify inspected pages. Persist bounded uploads only in ignored local runtime storage. No reference-building retrieval, CAD, 3D, auth, streaming, hosting or infrastructure expansion.

Authorized development exception: select the temporary OpenAI Responses adapter via AI_PROVIDER=openai while Gemini access is pending. It uses one structured sufficiency classification without a confidence score. The final sponsor demo uses AI_PROVIDER=gemini and native Gemini Decisions. All evidence and retry rules are shared; no automatic failover.

1. Bootstrap environment and establish API contract.
2. Independent plan/reliability review.
3. Backend: upload normalization, provenance, Gemini provider adapter, one sufficiency decision, one bounded unclear inspection, evidence-linked structured answers.
4. Frontend: source viewer, upload, ask, status, result/citation highlighting and clear operational errors.
5. Integration and independent implementation review; meaningful tests for unsupported answers, unclear handling, missing credentials, bad uploads, citation bounds and API failures.
6. Document and run the local workflow; live Gemini smoke test only when a Gemini credential is configured. No substitute provider without agreement.

The initial evidence gate is an experiment, not a correctness guarantee. Evaluate against standard Gemini using coverage, error among answered questions, unsupported answers, unnecessary abstention, latency and usage. Synthetic fixtures verify control flow, not model quality.
# API contract v1

Current drawing reconstruction is specified in [RECONSTRUCTION_V2_PLAN.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V2_PLAN.md) and [RECONSTRUCTION_V2_CONTRACT.md](RECONSTRUCTION_V2_CONTRACT.md). These supersede historical single-floor/relative-only restrictions; core evidence and provider invariants remain.

Root owns this contract; agents coordinate before changes. JSON uses snake_case.

The implemented 3D extension is specified in [3D_CONTRACT.md](3D_CONTRACT.md). Upload also accepts uncompressed IFC up to25MiB, with `kind` and `scene_url` fields; health adds `max_ifc_mb:25`. Answers add `highlight_ids` and `model_evidence`; IFC uses source records rather than page images. Existing drawing fields below remain compatible.

## Endpoints
- `GET /api/health`: `{status:"ok",provider_ready:bool,model:str,decision_model:str,limits:{max_upload_mb:10,max_pages:5}}`. Readiness means credentials/config exist, not verified provider access. No secrets.
- `POST /api/documents` multipart `file` (JPG/PNG/PDF, max 10 MiB, max 5 pages; reject larger documents rather than silently truncate). Returns `{document_id,filename,pages:[{page:1,width,height,image_url}],warnings:[]}`. Images are re-encoded PNG, PDF pages rendered. Opaque server-generated IDs; no filesystem paths.
- `GET /api/documents/{id}/pages/{page}` returns preview PNG.
- `POST /api/ask` JSON `{document_id,question}`. Question trimmed, 1–2000 chars. Returns Answer below.
- Standard errors: `{detail:"safe actionable message"}`; validation errors may be FastAPI detail arrays. API failures are 502/503, not insufficiency. Missing documents 404.

## Answer
```
{
  "status": "answered|insufficient|unclear",
  "answer": "human readable factual answer or scoped limitation",
  "evidence": [{"page":1,"bbox":[0.1,0.2,0.4,0.5],"label":"Bedroom label","observation":"MH annotation"}],
  "missing_information": ["Ceiling height"],
  "next_action": "Upload a section drawing with height dimensions.",
  "proposal": null,
  "inspected_pages": [1],
  "gate": {"decision":"sufficient|insufficient|unclear","confidence":0.8},
  "inspection_passes": 1,
  "usage": {"input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":0,"latency_ms":0}
}
```
`bbox` is [left,top,right,bottom], normalized 0–1 in the original displayed page. Validate positive area and page existence. Proposal if present: `{text, basis:"explicit_assumption|reference",reference:null|string}`. No invented reference buildings. Model-generated evidence is an aid to inspection, not a verified detection guarantee. # Voice interaction contract

Root owns this integration contract. Voice input/output augment the existing source-grounded question flow; they do not establish building facts.

## Endpoints

- `GET /api/voice/config`: `{transcription_ready,speech_ready,transcription_model,language_codes}`. Readiness means configuration is present, not successful provider access. Voice transcription uses Gemini independently of the selected QA provider.
- `GET /api/documents/{id}/voice-vocabulary`: `{terms:[str],rooms:[{id,name,floor_label}],warnings:[str]}`. Names come from cached room elements including geometry-less IFC records, plus floor names. Native floors can come from `Storey.Name`. Drawing names are fallible recognition hints and become available after reconstruction or generated-IFC reopening; no extra extraction request is made. Custom terms work before a scene exists. No generated dimensions or assumptions enter recognition or factual answering.
- WebSocket `/api/voice/transcribe`: initial JSON `{type:"start",document_id,custom_vocabulary:[str]}`. Server deduplicates building/custom vocabulary, validates document and configuration, opens Google, and emits `{type:"ready"}`. Client then streams signed little-endian PCM16 mono at 16 kHz as binary messages. AudioWorklet converts the actual browser sample rate. Server emits `{type:"transcript",text,final:boolean}`; finals append and interim text replaces the previous interim. Client `{type:"stop"}` flushes audio and waits for finalization; `{type:"cancel"}` or disconnect aborts. Google automatic activity detection is disabled: one recording uses `activity_start` before PCM and `activity_end` after the final PCM chunk. This avoids mistaking an earlier pause completion for Stop completion. The adapter keeps receiving across SDK receive loops and awaits the manual turn terminal acknowledgment. Successful completion emits `{type:"done"}`. Operational failures emit `{type:"error",message}` with safe text and preserve already received transcript text. Never treat a timeout as successful finalization.
- `POST /api/voice/speech`: `{document_id,text}` -> `audio/mpeg`, no-store. UI sends the exact displayed answer, including insufficient/unclear wording. No summarizer or new factual inference. Unknown documents return 404, missing configuration 503, upstream failures 502. Full MP3 is fetched before playback.

## Aliases and evidence

Aliases are user-defined, per-document browser-memory mappings to a selected room. Exact Unicode-boundary matching is case-insensitive, longest-first and nonrecursive. The UI shows the recognized text and editable canonical replacement before explicit Ask. Duplicate room names require floor qualification; duplicated name+floor targets are ambiguous and cannot receive an ID-specific alias through the text-only question API. Aliases and custom terms are hints, never evidence. The existing question endpoint, sufficiency gate, source citations and highlight validation remain authoritative.

## Lifecycle and limits

Only a user action opens the microphone. Recording and playback exclude one another. Stop, cancel, document replacement, new questions and page departure release microphone tracks, audio processing, sockets, pending synthesis and playback resources as appropriate. Delayed callbacks from an older recording/document cannot modify the current question or answer. Browser playback restrictions expose a manual playback fallback. Voice failures preserve ordinary text input, answers and citations.

Google documents at most 1,000 custom-vocabulary phrases; excess combined hints are explicitly rejected rather than truncated. There is no additional recording-duration or room-count cap. Configurable connection/finalization/synthesis deadlines release stalled operations; a finalization deadline reports incomplete transcription. Speech is limited to 6,000 characters, matching the original draft-answer bound; an expanded final answer may exceed that and remains text-only with a clear error, never silent truncation. Provider cancellation cannot reverse already billed work.
